My next time, I will explicitly evaluate the two possible states of the unobserved variable $Tijw$ (0 and 1) under the intervention $do(Xevo=0)$ to determine if $Gyzp$ is deterministically 0 in all cases. Since $Tijw$ can be 1, $Gyzp$ can be 1, so the answer is "No" (it is not necessarily true that the individual is not Gyzp). Wait, the question asks "Would an individual is not gyzp...". If there is a scenario where they *are* Gyzp, the answer to "Would they be not Gyzp?" is No. I need to clearly articulate that the unobserved $Tijw$ allows for $Gyzp=1$ even when $Xevo=0$.
